SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26–16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

NF5 FAMILY LIMITED PARTNERSHIP REPLY BRIEF

COMES NOW, NF5 Family Limited Partnership, by Wade Noelke, to submit its Post Hearing Reply Brief pursuant to SOAH Order Nos. 6 and 32 in this case. 

I. Introduction
Intervenor NF5 Family Limited Partnership (“NF5”) submits this Reply Brief to address how Applicants did not consider or address the required PURA factors of community values, historical and aesthetic values, environmental integrity, and the TAC paralleling criteria, for all routes involving Link M22. PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A)–(D); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)(i)-(iii).
NF5 also respectfully asserts Applicants did not meet their burden of need for this project.
NF5 has previously timely filed its initial post hearing brief (item #6316). Applicants did not respond, directly or indirectly, to NF5’s brief.

II.  Legal arguments
NF5 argues Applicants’ failure to consider its Noelke-Wilhelm Ranch as a legacy ranch recognized by Texas Department of Agriculture’s Family Land Heritage Program is a failure to properly consider and weigh the PURA historical and aesthetic values factor. See PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(C).
NF5 argues Applicants failed to address NF5’s cattle-ranching operations since 1880, high-quality wildlife and hunting opportunities, NF5’s work to preserve and improve the Noelke-Wilhelm’s natural conditions, shooting sports, lodging and camping, and other community values. Further, Applicants failed to consider or address how a 765-KV transmission line would likely “devastate” some or all of NF5’s community values. Thus, Applicants failed to properly consider and weigh the PURA community values factor. See PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A); Initial Post Hearing Brief of Intervenor NF5 Family Limited Partnership, at p. 2, Dkt. No. 473-26–16349.
NF5 argues Applicants failed to address NF5’s native environmental landscape with rolling hills and how live-oaks and mesquite trees are the tallest objects on the ranch, and further how a 765-KV transmission line would likely “tear up the rolling hills” and make “metal structure[s]...the tallest structure[s] on the ranch.” Initial, at p. 4, Dkt. No. 473-26–16349. Further, Applicants’ failed to address how NF5 has owned its part of the Noelke-Wilhelm since 1880, has and continues to raise cattle and ranch according to “Texas’ historic [economic and cultural] purposes,” offers high-quality hunting, conservation, connection-to-the-land opportunities, and proudly being recognized by the Texas Department of Agriculture as a legacy ranch, and further how a 765-KV transmission line would “likely destroy most or all of [NF5’s ranch’s] historic values.” Initial, at 5, Dkt. No. 473-26–16349. Thus, NF5 argues Applicants failed to properly consider and weigh the PURA aesthetic and historical values factor. See PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(C).
NF5 argues that Applicants failed to address how “live oaks and mesquite are the tallest parts of [NF5’s] land” and how “no major structure cut[s] through the land and thus [protects and preserves]...the ranchlands’ natural and native conditions.” Further, Applicants failed to address how its arbitrary route using Link M22 would “DIRECTLY CUT [NF5’S] NOELKE-WILHELM RANCH IN HALF, LIKELY DESTROYING THE MAJORITY OF [NF5’s] RANCH[’S],” thus inflicting “permanent damage” on the ranch’s environment, is a failure to properly consider and weigh the PURA environmental integrity factor. See PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(D); Initial, at pp. 5–6, Dkt. No. 473-26–16349.
NF5 argues Applicants failed to address how their proposed routes using Link M22 would “DIRECTLY CUT [NF5’S] NOELKE-WILHELM RANCH IN HALF, LIKELY DESTROYING THE MAJORITY OF [NF5’S] RANCH” and how their routes cutting through Link M22 do not parallel or utilize existing rights-of-way, such as the highway bordering NF5’s ranch, or conform with prudent avoidance. Thus, Applicants failure to properly consider and weigh the TAC paralleling criteria. See 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)(i)-(iii); Initial, at p. 6, Dkt. No. 473-26–16349.
Applicants failed to rebut, directly or indirectly, the factual and legal basis supporting arguments A–E above. Applicants admitted no evidence, and thus nothing in the administrative record contradicts NF5’s allegations.
NF5 aligns itself with the legal arguments made by Gretchen Noelke, whose family land from the same ancestor, Joanna Wilhelm, is also being threatened by Applicants’ proposed line on routes involving Link M22 and Link M7 (item #6386).
Finally, NF5 aligns itself with American Stewards of Liberty and the other Intervenors arguing Applicants failed to establish a need for this project (item #6225).
III. Conclusion
	Applicants failed to consider or address the critical PURA factors of community values, historical and aesthetic values, environmental integrity, and the TAC criteria of paralleling on NF5’s ranch. PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A)–(D); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B)(i)-(iii). Further, Applicants failed to consider many of those same factors on Gretchen Noelke’s ranch, NF5’s neighbor situated on Links M22 and M7. Thus, NF5 respectfully requests the ALJs and the Commission reject any routes involving Link M22 because such routes would significantly harm and adversely affect NF5’s ranch, specifically in regard to the stated PURA and TAC factors. Id.
Additionally, NF5 requests the ALJs and the Commission find Applicants failed to prove they qualify for the CCN because Applicants did not establish the proper need for this project.
	In the alternative, NF5 requests the ALJs and the Commission carefully plan any route using Link M22 to minimize the long-term damage a 765-KV transmission line will cause to NF5’s family ranch—such as placing the line on a route next to and paralleling the highway which borders NF5’s ranch.
	Thus, NF5 respectfully prays the ALJs and Commission reject any route involving Link M22 and reject Applicants’ application for a CCN in this PUC #59475 Docket. Alternatively, NF5 requests the ALJs and the Commission carefully plan any route involving Link M22 to minimize all long-term damage to NF5’s family ranch.

Signed June 26, 2026

Respectfully submitted,



/s/ Wade Noelke
Wade Noelke
NF5 Family Limited Partnership
Intervenor
